title: Bitcoin Investor: $15 XRP Price Is a Walk in the Park. We’re Aiming for $30
body: Bitcoin investor Btcbox123 believes XRP could eventually reach $30, suggesting that even a rally to $15 would represent only an initial milestone. Btcbox123 presented this outlook on X alongside a monthly XRP chart showing a large technical formation that has developed over several years. He described his projection as analysis rather than wishful thinking, pointing to the cryptocurrency’s historical price movements and converging trendlines as the basis for his bullish expectations. XRPの月足。これは願望ではありません。分析です。15＄は余裕で行く。目指すは30＄。いくぞXRPファミリー！ #XRP pic.twitter.com/6yy6YOhu1J — ₿₿ (@btcbox123) November 22, 2026 XRP Approaches The Convergence Of Two Major Trendlines Btcbox123’s monthly chart shows XRP trading within a large symmetrical triangle formed by a descending resistance line and an ascending support line. The upper yellow trendline connects previous price highs, while the lower boundary follows a series of higher lows established over several years. The chart captures several important stages in XRP’s price history . Following an initial surge, the cryptocurrency experienced a significant correction before recovering toward the descending resistance line. Another decline followed, but XRP gradually established higher lows, creating the upward-sloping support visible on the chart. The asset subsequently recorded another major rally, reaching approximately $3 before entering a corrective phase. Its price then declined toward the upper boundary of the larger formation, bringing it closer to the point where the two yellow trendlines converge. At the time of the chart’s capture, XRP traded at approximately $0.92441. Btcbox123’s technical drawing suggests that the cryptocurrency could make another upward move from this region as the formation approaches its narrower section. $30 Ultimate XRP Price Target The enthusiast accompanied the chart with an ambitious projection, writing: “This isn’t wishful thinking. It’s analysis. $15 is a walk in the park. We’re aiming for $30. Let’s go, XRP family!” His statement indicates that he expects XRP to record gains considerably larger than those represented by the $15 target . By identifying $30 as the ultimate objective, Btcbox123 is projecting a price level that would represent a substantial increase from XRP’s current valuation. The white projection drawn on the chart illustrates his expectations. It traces a potential upward movement from the current price region, followed by an extended rally toward the $12 area and beyond. Although the drawing does not establish a specific timeline, it communicates his expectation of a significant bullish expansion. Other Analysts Maintain Higher XRP Price Expectations Btcbox123’s projection also comes as other market commentators examine XRP’s long-term technical structure. Analyst Zayro previously compared XRP’s monthly chart with its 2017 pre-breakout structure. His analysis identified ascending support and price compression as important features, with potential targets at $5, $10, and $15 if the trendline continues to hold. However, Google Gemini’s assessment of XRP’s December price outlook presented a more cautious near-term picture. Its base-case projection placed the cryptocurrency between $0.88 and $0.96, while its bullish scenario identified $1.02 to $1.10 as a potential range. While these forecasts differ considerably in their price expectations, Btcbox123 remains confident in XRP’s long-term upside potential. title: TSMC's Potential $22.6 Billion Texas Chip Factory Hinges on Tax Breaks
body: Key takeaways TSMC proposes a $22.6 billion Texas semiconductor facility Property tax incentives could determine the investment decision Factory would manufacture advanced 2nm chips or smaller Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (N YSE: TSM ) is considering a $22.6 billion semiconductor manufacturing facility in Brazos County, Texas, as the world's largest contract chipmaker evaluates further expansion of its US production capacity. According to an application submitted to Texas authorities, property tax incentives could determine whether the company proceeds with the project or expands its existing manufacturing infrastructure in Arizona instead. The potential investment comes as growing demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to support TSMC's US manufacturing expansion , despite uncertainty across global semiconductor markets. TSMC Seeks Tax Incentives for $22.6 Billion Factory TSMC Arizona Corporation submitted its application under the Texas Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation (JETI) program, which provides eligible businesses with temporary school district property tax limitations. The accompanying economic assessment estimates a total investment of $22.62 billion, including $8.60 billion in real property and $14.02 billion in personal property. The proposed facility could support 2,099 direct jobs. Construction could begin in 2027, with completion and commercial operations targeted for 2031. The requested incentive period would extend from 2032 through 2041. TSMC described the tax limitation as a ”determinative and compelling factor” in its investment decision, citing the economic advantages of expanding its established Arizona operations. The company has entered preliminary agreements related to potential land acquisitions, but these arrangements do not constitute a final commitment to the Texas location. Texas Factory Could Produce Next-Generation AI Chips The proposed manufacturing campus would produce advanced logic semiconductors using 2-nanometer or smaller manufacturing technologies. These processors could support AI accelerators, high-performance computing systems and next-generation mobile devices, potentially expanding domestic manufacturing capacity for US technology companies. The investment also comes amid increasing efforts to diversify semiconductor supply chains. Recent US chip export restrictions have added further complexity to the industry's international operations. TSMC has separately explored reducing its dependence on Chinese rare-earth components used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Although the Texas facility could strengthen domestic chip production, its application does not identify specific future customers or supply agreements. AI Demand Drives TSMC's Expanding Capital Budget TSMC's potential Texas investment follows another period of strong financial growth driven by demand for advanced semiconductor technologies. According to its third-quarter financial results , the company generated $46.72 billion in revenue, representing a 41.2% annual increase. Management maintained its 2026 capital expenditure budget of between $60 billion and $64 billion. The company also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion. However, overseas manufacturing expansion introduces additional operating costs. TSMC expects its international facilities to dilute gross margins by three to four percentage points in the coming years. These expenses remain particularly relevant as global AI stocks face renewed selling pressure , despite continued growth in semiconductor demand.

title: Stellar Price Analysis: XLM's $0.11 Floor Decides December After a 28% Monthly Slide
body: Three Things to Know Stellar pulled in more real-world asset tokens than any other major blockchain over the past month. The daily chart shows XLM deeply oversold, yet momentum still favors the sellers. One floor near $0.11 now stands between the token and open air below. Stellar has become the busiest chain for new tokenized real-world assets. Its token has gone the other way, falling for weeks. That gap leaves XLM holders with a hard question heading into December. Can network adoption finally pull buyers back to the coin? So far it has not, and the chart now hinges on a single support level. Stellar Tops the Tokenization League While Its Token Bleeds Stellar led every major blockchain in net real-world asset token inflows in the last 30 days, according to RWA.xyz data dated November 24. The network added about $1.2 billion, measured as tokens minted minus tokens burned. That was more than double the next chain on the list. Injective followed with $525 million. Base drew $347 million, BNB Chain took in $326 million and Robinhood added $147 million. Ethereum moved the other way. It posted the largest net outflow at $1.4 billion, while Avalanche lost $191 million and Aptos shed $101 million. By total tokenized value, Stellar ranks fourth at $4.9 billion. Ethereum leads with $14.3 billion, ahead of BNB Chain at $6 billion and Solana at $5.1 billion. XRPL trails Stellar at $3 billion. The token tells a different story. XLM carries a market cap of about $4.61 billion, and sellers have kept the upper hand. Daily volume climbed more than 85% to around $154 million as the selling hit. Real assets are flowing onto Stellar, but that demand has not reached the coin. Both Key Averages Now Sit Far Above XLM Stellar (XLM) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView XLM changed hands near $0.12 at the latest check, down about 5% over the past day. The drop extends a slide that has run for weeks. The token is off about 11% over seven days and roughly 28% over 30 days. Each timeframe is worse than the one before it, which is the pattern of a market that keeps finding new sellers. That monthly decline has also widened since the tokenization data came out. The token traded near $0.13 on November 24. Its 30-day loss then stood at about 24%. The extra slippage since then shows the inflow headlines did little to stem the selling. Moving averages help explain the setup. A moving average smooths out daily noise by tracking the average closing price over a set number of days. The 50-day average sits near $0.16. The 200-day average is higher, around $0.18. XLM trades well under both lines. When price sits below these averages, they tend to act as ceilings that turn rallies back. The shorter average also sits below the longer one, which confirms the trend points down on both time horizons. That leaves XLM in a clean downtrend with no sign yet of a turn. For now, traders treat network growth and coin price as separate stories. Sellers Stay in Charge Even at Oversold Extremes RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 28. Readings under 30 count as oversold, meaning the selling has run hard and fast. Stretches like this often come before a relief bounce. An oversold reading does not mark a bottom by itself, though. Prices can stay oversold for days while sellers keep pressing, and a weak trend can grind lower from here. Other gauges back that caution. The MACD, which tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line, so momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings show a real trend in place, and sellers are the ones driving it. A lasting bounce usually needs momentum to turn first, with the MACD crossing back above its signal line. Until then, oversold readings mostly show the decline is stretched. One Floor Left Under the Price Support sits near $0.11, and the data shows no clear level below it. A close under that floor would leave XLM with no obvious place for buyers to step in. Holding that line keeps the oversold setup in play. On the upside, the first hurdle is resistance near $0.14. A move back above it would give XLM its first higher high in weeks. That would be the earliest sign the downtrend is losing grip. The next barrier sits around $0.15. Any relief rally would run into the zone where the token broke down earlier. Traders who bought there may sell to get out even, which could cap the bounce. Where the Next Three Days Could Take XLM Two paths stand out, and both hinge on the same floor. Bullish: XLM holds $0.11 and posts a daily close above $0.14. That would open a run toward $0.15. The setup fails if price closes below $0.11. Bearish: A close under the floor extends the slide into territory with no marked support. Sellers would then set the pace. This view fails if XLM closes back above $0.14. Adoption Has Yet to Pay the Token Holders Stellar keeps winning on adoption, and the token has yet to share in it. Patient traders may want to see the floor hold and momentum turn before stepping in. The risk sits below that floor. With no mapped support underneath, a break could move fast. Disclaimer: This article is provided for informational purposes only. title: Why is Bitcoin down today? BTC drops below $60,000 as ETF outflows mount
body: Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, wiping out Monday's spike on Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, as outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs ran into a fifth day. Bitcoin traded at $59,444.78, down 7.9% from Monday's high of $64,533.96. What happened to Bitcoin today? Bitcoin hit $64,533.96 at 14:27 UK time on Monday, about half an hour after Nvidia's announcement. It has since given back the whole move and more. The price first slipped below $60,000 at 02:59 UK time on Tuesday. It fell to a low of $59,249.12 at 16:36 UK time, below the $61,060.48 it traded at just before the Nvidia news. Coinbase's 24-hour figures showed a 4.4% fall at 16:57 UK time. Ether was down 2.3% at $1,668.33, XRP 3.0% at $0.9109, Solana 4.1% at $69.01 and Dogecoin 2.8% at $0.05473. Bitcoin chart | Source: Coinbase Why is Bitcoin falling? The clearest pressure is coming from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Data from Farside Investors show net outflows of $569.7 million on Monday, 23 November, led by BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which lost $509.3 million. It was the fifth straight session of outflows. November outflows have now reached $4.71 billion, the biggest monthly total in Farside's records since the funds launched in January 2024. The previous largest was $4.51 billion in June 2026. Leverage has added to the swings. CoinGlass data showed $454.44 million of crypto liquidations over 24 hours, with $376.63 million of them being long positions. Bitcoin accounted for $160.64 million. Over the past 12 hours, long positions made up $175.57 million of the $215.69 million liquidated. Wider risk appetite also cooled after Monday's rally. Nasdaq Composite was down 1.66% and Nvidia shares fell 7.39%. What happens next? Bitcoin has traded either side of $60,000 for most of Tuesday, with today's $59,249.12 low the nearest marker. On Saturday, 21 November, it fell as low as $55,106 on Coinbase. Traders will also watch whether ETF outflows continue when Tuesday's flow data are published after the US close. There was some support elsewhere. Strategy on Monday said that it bought 457 BTC for $29.6 million between 16 and 22 November, taking its holdings to 851,305 BTC. Separately, CFTC staff said on 23 November that derivatives exchanges and clearing houses may count Bitcoin and Ether towards some financial resources requirements, subject to haircuts. Should you buy Bitcoin now? Bitcoin has swung by more than $5,000 in less than 24 hours, a reminder of how volatile crypto can be. title: Sky’s $159M lending pool shows zero cash for withdrawals
body: BitcoinWorld Sky’s $159M lending pool shows zero cash for withdrawals Sky Protocol’s stUSDS lending pool held about $159 million in assets on Nov. 23, 2026, yet depositors could withdraw practically nothing, according to Crypto.news . The squeeze became public the same day Sky co-founder Rune Christensen, posting from @RuneKek at 13:39 UTC, disclosed that he had repaid 3 million USDS and still owed about 77 million, and wrote that the situation was “on me.” Sky’s stUSDS pool reported almost $159 million in assets on Nov. 23, 2026, but virtually no USDS available for withdrawal because nearly all funds were on loan. Co-founder Rune Christensen said he had repaid 3 million USDS and still owed about 77 million, and said he was exploring a direct SKY sale to institutional investors to repay the rest. Key facts The pool’s dashboard showed roughly $158.7 million in total value and 99.99% utilization by 9:04 a.m. Eastern on Nov. 23, with no liquidity displayed for users. Christensen’s outstanding debt of about 77 million USDS was close to half the pool’s size at that snapshot, after his reported 3 million USDS repayment. An Ethereum transaction record shows a redemption of roughly 910,000 USDS in the same block as the repayment, about 30% of the amount just paid back. Sky’s staking analytics showed borrowing and deposit rates near 50% annualized on Nov. 23. A Nov. 23 forum post by user misher proposed lowering the annual rate to about 10%, pausing new borrowing and buying stUSDS with reserves at up to $7 million a month. Why the pool could look full and still be empty stUSDS is not a simple deposit receipt. Users supply USDS, the stablecoin that grew out of MakerDAO’s rebrand, and receive stUSDS in return; that cash funds loans backed by staked SKY and earns a variable rate tied to borrowing. Loans still outstanding sit inside the pool’s reported assets, but only unborrowed USDS can meet redemptions. When utilization nears 100%, a large headline balance and a zero withdrawal reading describe the same pool at the same moment. The same-block sequence illustrates how thin the buffer was. Christensen’s repayment returned 3 million USDS to the pool, and a 910,000 USDS redemption left in the same block, per Crypto.news’ review of the Ethereum record. The cash did not sit idle; it was claimed. That also tempers the effect of any institutional token sale Christensen arranges. A small placement would likely fund only a short redemption window, with the benefit depending on proceeds and on how much withdrawal demand piled up while the pool was fully lent out. What the governance debate is really about The Nov. 23 forum proposal from misher would cut borrowing costs, halt new draws against staked SKY and let the protocol buy stUSDS in the secondary market until a threshold of 0.98 is reached. Commenters pressed on that number: one, posting as Animatronix, asked whether 0.98 meant 0.98 USDS per token or 98% of net asset value, which they put at about 1.09 USDS at the time. At an illustrative 1.09 NAV, 98% works out to roughly 1.0682 USDS, against 0.98 USDS for a flat price. A separate thread of the discussion, led by a participant posting as ares, asked who receives whatever cash comes back. Ares backed the borrowing pause and market purchases but wanted rate cuts tied to mandatory repayment schedules, proposing a 20% rate for borrowers who meet the timetable and 50% for those who miss it. The distinction matters: a lower rate makes debt cheaper to carry without deciding when principal returns, and depositors waiting to exit would also accrue less. Distributing incoming cash proportionally or through a queue would produce different outcomes for holders than open redemption. Why it matters The episode exposes a concentration risk that exists quietly in many DeFi credit pools: one large borrower can determine whether everyone else can leave. USDS can keep trading near its peg while stUSDS redemption stalls, because the peg measures the stablecoin and liquidity measures the pool’s cash. Sky is still working through its USDS reserve picture after a $2 billion swap, as we reported in our coverage of Sky’s USDC reserve falling to $867 million . The market has taken note: SKY was quoted at $0.0378 on Nov. 24, down 29.3% over seven days. Market snapshot At the 16:46 UTC snapshot on Nov. 24, 2026, CoinPaprika data listed SKY at $0.0378 (₹3.51), down 8.5% in 24 hours and 29.3% over seven days, with a market capitalization of $880.1 million and 24-hour volume of $13.7 million. Bitcoin traded at $59,437 (₹5,515,427), down 4.0% on the day and 6.9% on the week. What to watch Christensen said he would post updates at least every 48 hours, so the next disclosed balance and any on-chain transfers reducing his positions are the clearest signal. Two other data points matter: whether the dashboard shows cash surviving after material repayments, and whether governance puts a formal vote on the rate cut, borrowing pause and reserve-funded purchases with an explicit price benchmark. Frequently Asked Questions What is the Sky stUSDS pool? It is a Sky Protocol lending module where users supply USDS, the protocol’s stablecoin, and receive stUSDS in return. Those deposits fund loans secured by staked SKY and accrue a variable rate tied to borrowing demand. How can a pool hold $159 million and still run out of withdrawal cash? Outstanding loans count toward the pool’s assets, but only unborrowed USDS can cover immediate redemptions. With utilization near 100%, the dashboard showed no cash available even though the pool’s headline value was large. Who borrowed from the pool? Sky co-founder Rune Christensen disclosed about 77 million USDS of outstanding debt after repaying 3 million. In a Nov. 23 post he took responsibility, writing that the situation was on him. What did the Nov. 23 governance proposal suggest? A forum post by user misher proposed cutting the annual rate to about 10%, pausing new borrowing against staked SKY, and using reserves to buy stUSDS on the open market with roughly $7 million a month in potential funding. Did Christensen’s repayment restore withdrawal liquidity? Only briefly. An Ethereum record shows a redemption of roughly 910,000 USDS in the same block as the repayment, and by 9:04 a.m. Eastern the dashboard again displayed zero available liquidity. title: XRP, Cardano, Polygon Face Brutal Snub as Crypto Executive Exposes Why He’s Avoiding These Altcoins in 2026
body: Are Ripple’s XRP , Cardano (ADA) , and Polygon (POL) losing their appeal among crypto investors in 2026? Ben Simpson, founder of crypto investment platform Collective Shift, has named all three among six altcoins he says he wouldn’t touch with a 10-foot pole, citing concerns ranging from weak network activity and questionable valuations to intensifying competition. His blunt assessment raises fresh questions about which altcoins have the strongest fundamentals to survive the increasingly competitive crypto market. Simpson Questions XRP’s Value Proposition for Token Holders In his post on X , Simpson acknowledged XRP’s role in enabling near-instant, inexpensive payments on the XRP Ledger but argued that the token lacks a compelling mechanism for capturing the value generated by Ripple’s business growth. XRP enables fast, low-cost payments on the XRP Ledger. My issue with XRP is it's "value capture". When a business grows, I want to see how that success benefits the token I'm holding. In this case, there is none. Ripple can grow its revenue, but holders don't receive those… — Ben Simpson (@bensimpsonau) November 22, 2026 His main concern is that Ripple’s commercial success does not necessarily translate into direct financial benefits for XRP holders. Even as the San Francisco-headquartered company expands its revenue and boosts its payment operations, investors do not receive a share of those profits. He also pointed out that Ripple does not use its business earnings to buy back XRP, a mechanism that could potentially create additional demand for the token. For Simpson, the absence of both profit-sharing and a buyback program makes it difficult to establish a direct link between Ripple’s growing business and XRP’s price in the long term. He considers these shortcomings significant enough to keep XRP off his investment list, despite the network’s payment capabilities. Cardano’s Weak Network Activity Despite Billion-Dollar Valuation Raises Concerns Simpson also expressed reservations about Cardano, arguing that its adoption level does not justify its market valuation. Although ADA powers a blockchain designed to support smart contracts and decentralized applications, he believes the network is generating relatively little economic activity compared with its overall market size. To support his argument, Simpson pointed to Cardano’s fee generation, claiming that the network collected just $140,000 in transaction fees over a 30-day period despite ADA carrying a market capitalization of approximately $7.5 billion. For him, the disparity raises questions about whether Cardano is attracting enough users and developers to sustain its valuation. He believes a blockchain with such a substantial market capitalization should demonstrate considerably stronger usage and demand for its services. Ultimately, Simpson’s concern is that Cardano needs to translate its technological ambitions and established ecosystem into greater real-world activity. Without a meaningful increase in network usage, he appears unconvinced that ADA offers an attractive investment proposition. Polygon Faces Mounting Competition as Rivals Challenge Its Scaling Advantage Polygon also made the list, with concerns centered on the growing competition in Ethereum’s scaling ecosystem. Although POL supports a network designed to make transactions faster and cheaper, the increasing number of competing blockchain solutions has made it harder for Polygon to maintain a distinctive advantage. Simpson’s concern is that newer networks are offering similar benefits, including lower transaction costs and faster processing speeds, leaving Polygon with fewer obvious ways to differentiate itself. With several projects competing for developers, users, and blockchain activity, POL faces the challenge of proving why it deserves a place ahead of its rivals. Sui, Ronin, and Dogwifhat Also Fail to Make the Cut Beyond XRP, Cardano, and Polygon, three other cryptocurrencies also fell short of Ben Simpson’s investment criteria: Sui (SUI), Ronin (RON), and Dogwifhat (WIF). Unlike his concerns about the first three crypto projects, his reservations about these tokens stem largely from changing investment convictions, disappointing adoption, and excessive reliance on market hype. Sui was among the projects Simpson previously held before changing his investment outlook. The high-speed blockchain is designed to support decentralized applications and transactions, but he eventually dumped his SUI holdings at a loss of between 20% and 30% after his investment thesis changed. He did not elaborate on the specific developments that prompted his decision. Ronin was another project he abandoned after its growth failed to match his expectations. Initially attracted by the potential of blockchain gaming, the pundit bought into the network, which uses RON for transaction fees and staking. However, the anticipated expansion in gaming adoption did not materialize as he had hoped, prompting him to exit the position relatively quickly. He argued that strong sector potential means little without meaningful retail participation. WIF, meanwhile, represented a different kind of investment mistake. Simpson admitted that his decision to buy the Solana-based meme coin was driven largely by hype rather than underlying fundamentals. After his investment thesis changed, he sold his holdings to limit further losses. His experience with WIF appears to have reinforced his preference for cryptocurrencies backed by stronger fundamentals rather than speculative excitement.

title: 20% Minimum Cut As CFTC Staff Lets Exchanges Count Bitcoin Toward Reserves
body: CFTC staff said Monday that US derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins toward reserves covering at least 12 months of operating costs. Staff require a minimum 20% discount on Bitcoin and Ether and a minimum 2% discount on qualifying stablecoins. Operators can use crypto for the operating reserve, but they must hold separate assets to meet their liquidity requirements. The CFTC announcement also covers venues where parties arrange swaps. An operator holding $1 of Bitcoin at market value can credit no more than 80 cents of it toward the yearlong operating reserve. The same limit applies to Ether. Staff set the discounts to account for the risk of holding crypto while meeting the requirement. The 12-month reserve covers operating costs. A separate liquidity rule requires assets that an operator can use readily, such as cash or highly liquid securities. The CFTC said crypto assets, including payment stablecoins, do not qualify as cash or highly liquid securities under US accounting standards. Operators cannot count those crypto holdings toward the separate liquidity requirement. Swap trading venues must hold at least three months of operating costs in unencumbered liquid assets, meaning assets that have not been pledged elsewhere. Derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses must hold at least six months of operating costs in those assets. Counting Bitcoin toward the 12-month operating reserve does not reduce either liquidity minimum. The CFTC’s Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued the advisory. It gives regulated operators more flexibility in what they count toward operating reserves without changing the liquidity assets they must hold. The Commission has not approved the advisory as a formal rule change, and it creates no new rules or enforceable rights. The advisory represents the views of staff only.
